correctness.rationale: Theorem A (M_3(2,7)=15) verified end-to-end. Independent replay of wit7.json/wit8.json with two separate implementations confirms: PG(2,7) N=57 and PG(2,8) N=73 incidence rebuilt from scratch; max line occupancy 3 (no 4-secant); spectra [12,0,15,30] and [12,18,12,31] satisfy sum n_i=N and sum i*n_i=k(q+1) (120=15*8, 135=15*9); 0 uncovered outside points (42/42 and 58/58 covered by 3-secants), hence complete/maximal under inclusion; NMDS distributions sum to q^3 with distance k-3. Upper-bound proof checked line-by-line: cap k<=2q+3 from q+1 lines through P (k<=17 at q=7, k<=19 at q=8) is valid; at q=7, k=16 forces unique (t,s)=(7,1) and k=17 forces (8,0) — exhaustively confirmed no other nonnegative solutions — so every P lies on exactly t 3-secants and 3*t_3=k*t forces 3|k*t; 16*7=112 and 17*8=136 both =1 mod 3, impossible, closing k<=15. Witness at 15 closes equality. No search needed; no gap. Theorem B interval k<=19 follows from same cap; q=8 k=18 (8,1,144 divisible) and k=19 (9,0,171 divisible) correctly left open, and DRAFT honestly labels q=8 stochastic plateau as conjecture/evidence, not proof.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors substantively disjoint. (1) Bartoli-Marcugini-Pambianco 2012 (arXiv:1201.2260) is the only exact (n,3)-arc packing found and solves only q=16 (max 28/min 15) — same problem class but different order, leaves q=7,8 untouched. (2) Marcugini-Milani-Pambianco 2010 (arXiv:1005.3412) and Bartoli-Davydov et al. FOP tables (arXiv:1404.0469) concern (k,2)-arcs (no 3 collinear, 2-secant completeness) and t_2 minima/upper bounds — different object (allows exactly 3, forbids 4), different completeness (3-secant covering), does not imply M_3 values, spectra, or 3|k*t UNSAT. (3) Korchmaros-Nagy-Szonyi 2023 (arXiv:2302.10162) proves completeness of large Hermitian/BKS (k,q+1)-arcs for r>=4 via Galois/Hasse-Weil — asymptotic, explicitly leaves small-q boundary open. Live arXiv searches for '(k,3)-arc PG(2,7)' (no results) and 'complete (n,3)-arc' (only q=16 hit) confirm no tabled M_3(2,7)/M_3(2,8), spectra, or UNSAT logs. Internal SCOPE013 (conic-plus (17,3)-arc in PG(2,9) within-family) and SCOPE020/025 (3D caps, PG(2,4) incidence) are disjoint objects. Claim is new, not renamed implementation or parameter substitution.

value.rationale: Strongest headline M_3(2,7)=15 is a rigorously proved exact invariant of a natural object motivated before computation: Korchmaros et al. abstract frames small complete (k,n)-arcs with few characters and k near plane order as rare/hard with finite-geometry/coding applications; q=16 (n,3)-arc max/min precedent establishes exact finite (n,3) boundaries as citable; q=7 is the natural first odd order. Value was not known or mechanically implied (no table; cap k<=2q+3 alone gives 17, closure needs divisibility + witness). Exact spectrum (12,0,15,30) and [15,3,12] NMDS reading give the precise fact a future researcher calibrating the small-(k,n)-arc program or q-ary code tables would retrieve. Narrowness (one order) does not disqualify per standard. Incomplete q=8 census is honestly limited to record+interval k<=19 and does not erase the closed headline.
